units.spine: A stranger new to Hochhausen finds the market without being told the way, because the road carrying the most people through the place runs straight to it.
Professional hands keep the town safe, paid through Hochhausen's charter hall rather than left to luck and neighbours.
Here in Hochhausen, money is settled enough that people argue about other things.
What the town needs, it can get, and what it makes, it can move.
Whatever Hochhausen could hold, it could hold only briefly.
The town could hold against the trouble it expects, and admits it is no proof against the trouble it does not.
Nothing at Hochhausen is organised against what lives beyond the fields, and each household answers for its own fences.
The complaint book here holds more entries opened than closed.
A careful eye passing through Hochhausen notices first that nothing here is spare.
No practitioner keeps a place in Hochhausen, no arrangement stands for one, and no one expects either to appear.
The town's food security rests on its own harvest, proof against a closed road but not against a bad year.
A single day in Hochhausen gives no sign that The Commercial Circle and The Administrative Circle are at odds, and the sign only shows on the second day.
Goods come into Hochhausen and goods go out of it, and neither is remarkable.
The town sits on a road and lives off it, with goods coming in, goods going out, and people passing through.
Hochhausen is the size a village of its kind settles at, and it has settled there.
One tie matters to Hochhausen more than any other, and that weight shows in what the town does and what it does not.
The people here are tied to their neighbours the way people in any settled place are, and there is nothing more particular to say about it.
A close look at Hochhausen turns up one loose end, the kind a single institution could tie off.
